ambiguities:
I02: the draw generator yields region indices only, and no file this round may read records which region each index names. I took the regions in Python sorted() order. On all five problems this equals the order in which the regions first appear in the rows (sorted by row) and in sample.parquet; for defo, fire, pm25 and ndvi it also equals the export manifest's groups. The matrix itself is reproduced exactly by int.from_bytes(SHA-256('shap_v1|AW4|

|0||')[:8], 'big') mod G.

I04: the protocol does not name the record that holds 'the lead's test set'. I used the rivals' export of each headline run: D:\treeroute\rival_export\

\\lead_0\test\*.parquet. Its row count equals counts.test and the rivals' 'every test row'. I read only unit, time, issue and the candidate x__ columns.

C16/X02: calendar takes one value per time step, so it literally meets the global-index rule. I gave precedence to the families named by their columns (normal, hist_*, calendar and ctx:*) before the global-index test.

C15/X03: section 8 asks for a family-share distance in 'every pair, both levels', but families are built from variable-level phi. The feature-level pairs therefore carry the same family TV as the variable-level pairs.

C07: J, B1's pair J and the determined signs are fixed at the full sample. The top-k sets and their unions are found again on each draw. Section 10 says this choice should follow compare_shap.py's, which I was not allowed to see.
C08/C20: n_J and stability get no interval. n_nonzero and the sign counts do (recomputed per draw, so percentile ends can be non-integers).

C23: I read 'the median rival' as the median of the rivals' own-history shares. A rival is named only when the count is odd and one rival attains the median: none for coral (all zero) or NDVI (4 rivals).
C25: section 8 says 'for every arcsine-link model ... (fire)'. I covered coral's four arcsine models as well as fire's treeroute.
C09: 'nonzero' read as I > 0 over the model's own columns. This matches meta.json players_nonzero / variables_nonzero in every piece.
C17: sign agreement is undefined (null) when no player of the union is determined in both models. This happens for fire's four feature-level treeroute pairs and for three NDVI BARDL pairs.
C10: the tie-break name is the player name with its x__/c__ prefix, compared in Python code-point order (upper case before lower case).
surprises: Defo B1 is exactly the main run: the rows.parquet and background_keys.parquet files are byte-identical.

Under B1 the seasonal normal dominates, as section 5 anticipates. It is the top variable on fire (share 0.54), pm25 (0.44) and ndvi (0.32), and its family share is 0.81, 0.70 and 0.44; under B2 it is exactly 0. The family-share TV between the main run and B1 is 0.81, 0.70 and 0.49.
Fire, feature level: treeroute's sign agreement with every rival is undefined on the full sample and on all 2,000 draws. None of the top-10 union players has a determined sign in both models.
pm25 main row: the median top-20-union Spearman of treeroute against its rivals is about -0.02, while Spearman over J is about 0.85. NDVI's ranges from -0.41 to 0.38.

NDVI: BARDL's ties make the identity (mW-1)/(m-1) fail badly. At the feature level W = 0.418, (mW-1)/(m-1) = 0.273, and the direct mean pairwise Spearman is 0.246. BARDL's share TV to the other models is 0.88 to 0.99.
Coral's only structural zero is normal; the protocol's smoke note had expected normal plus four constant cyclone columns. Coral has no own-history variable, so every own-history share there is 0.
Coral's test set: 264 of its 793 day steps hold a single visit, where any column trivially takes one value. Still, only nino34a passes the global-index rule.
NDVI's x__epo_lag12 has missing test-set values, but only at steps where every unit is missing; ignoring missing values gives the same global indices on all five problems.
Fire treeroute's pre is greater than 0 on only 226 of the 1,000 sample rows (77.4% zero), in 27 of 40 regions. The protocol quotes 75.4% over all rows.
pm25's B1 pair J includes conflict_events, which treeroute's main run gives exactly 0.
No row is flagged by S-RESID in any of the 29 pieces, so choice C01 changes nothing.
